original_question: Let R = (R_1, ..., R_n) be the vectorial Riesz transform. Is the endpoint Lorentz-space estimate ||f||_{L^{(p,∞)}}^{p-1} <= C ||Σ_{α=1}^n R_α(|Rf|^{p-2} R_α f)||_{L^{(p',∞)}} valid?
target_in_paper: Problem 3.2 in Section 3.1.3, introduced as a reformulation of the unknown left-hand-side estimate (3.4) at the endpoint Lorentz choice X=L(n,∞) and Y=L(n,1). ([mimuw.edu.pl](https://www.mimuw.edu.pl/~pawelst/assets/pdf/1606.07891v1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper: it reproduces the vectorial Riesz transform R=(R_1,\dots,R_n), the exact nonlinear expression \sum_{\alpha=1}^n R_\alpha(|Rf|^{p-2}R_\alpha f), the weak Lorentz norms on both sides, and the left-hand exponent p-1. ([mimuw.edu.pl](https://www.mimuw.edu.pl/~pawelst/assets/pdf/1606.07891v1.pdf))
missing_details: State that the paper poses this as an open 'true or false' problem, not as a proved estimate.
Specify the ambient setting: the standard Riesz transforms on Euclidean space \mathbb{R}^n.
Define the exponent range 1<p<\infty and the Hölder conjugate p'=p/(p-1).
Define |Rf| as the Euclidean norm |Rf|=(\sum_{\alpha=1}^n |R_\alpha f|^2)^{1/2}.

Make the quantifier explicit: ask whether there exists a constant C=C(n,p)>0 such that the estimate holds for every scalar test function f in a natural class (for a stand-alone formulation, Schwartz functions are the cleanest choice).

Record the paper-specific context: this estimate is introduced because the left-hand-side bound (3.4) is unknown for X=L(n,∞) and Y=L(n,1), and the application of chief interest in the paper is the case p=n.
refined_question: For a fixed dimension n\ge 2 and exponent 1<p<\infty, let p'=p/(p-1), and let R=(R_1,\dots,R_n) be the standard vectorial Riesz transform on \mathbb{R}^n, defined on Schwartz functions by \widehat{R_\alpha f}(\xi)=-i\xi_\alpha|\xi|^{-1}\widehat f(\xi). Writing |Rf|=(\sum_{\alpha=1}^n |R_\alpha f|^2)^{1/2}, is it true or false that there exists a constant C=C(n,p)>0 such that every scalar Schwartz function f on \mathbb{R}^n satisfies \|f\|_{L^{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)}^{p-1}\le C\left\|\sum_{\alpha=1}^n R_\alpha\big(|Rf|^{p-2}R_\alpha f\big)\right\|_{L^{p',\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)}?

justification: The draft clearly targets Problem 3.2 rather than any Section 1 statement. Section 3.1.1 sets up the abstract regularity scheme via the left-hand-side estimate (3.4) and right-hand-side estimate (3.5). Section 3.1.3 then explains that Lorentz-space bookkeeping for the H-system forces the endpoint choice Y=L(n,1) and hence X=L(n,∞), and says that the resulting missing estimate is reformulated as Problem 3.2. The paper immediately adds that the problem is easy for p=2, that the strong-space analogue with L^p and L^{p'} follows by the same duality idea, and that nearby non-endpoint Lorentz analogues are known when one perturbs away from p. Later, in Section 4, the authors explicitly refer back to Problem 3.2 as one of the remaining obstructions in the antisymmetric-potential model. ([mimuw.edu.pl](https://www.mimuw.edu.pl/~pawelst/assets/pdf/1606.07891v1.pdf))
